Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the NovaMart, Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to NovaMart's Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Thompson, CEO; Michael Chen, CFO; Lisa Patel, COO; David Kim, CMO; Elena Vasquez, CTO; and Raj Singh, CDO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, CEO of NovaMart.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q2 performance, driven by robust active buyer growth through effective user acquisition and retention, alongside the effectiveness of our marketing campaigns boosting brand awareness. We saw significant growth in key metrics like GMV up 25% year-over-year to $3.2 billion and active buyers reaching 28.7 million.

Our focus remains on optimizing order frequency by evolving customer purchasing habits toward more repeat engagement. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our NovaPrime subscription service, which we believe will significantly enhance customer lifetime value.

We are investing heavily in seller services and value-added offerings to drive higher-margin revenue streams.

We are focused on improving operating expense efficiency while scaling operations.

We are expanding our presence in high-growth regions like APAC and LATAM.

Finally, we are committed to navigating seasonality impacts through data-driven inventory and promotion strategies.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Chen, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. Our Q2 revenue was $2.3 billion, an increase of 22% year-over-year. Gross margin was 43.8%, driven by a favorable product mix shift toward private labels, supply chain efficiencies, and reduced fulfillment costs as a percentage of GMV. Let me unpack that gross margin trend in detail. This quarter's consolidated gross margin expanded 210 basis points year-over-year to 43.8%, and on a trailing 12-month basis, it's now at 42.9%, up from 39.7% last year. This marks the fifth straight quarter of improvement, thanks to our disciplined execution on product mix, logistics, supplier terms, and pricing.

Visually, if you look at our investor deck slide 12, you'll see the steady climb from the 38.5% trough in Q3 2022. The H1 acceleration—from 41.2% in Q1—comes largely from private labels now at 28% of GMV, delivering mid-50s margins versus third-party averages in the mid-30s. We've shifted toward higher-margin categories like beauty and electronics, up 22% year-over-year, adding 320 basis points, while pruning low-margin apparel. Our AI assortment engine reallocates inventory based on LTV projections, lifting AOV to $68.

Fulfillment costs improved to 12.4% of revenue from 14.1%, with robotic systems in 15 North American centers cutting cycle times 35% and enabling 18% same-day delivery. We've secured carrier contracts below spot rates, hedging Red Sea issues. Supplier sourcing from Vietnam and Mexico saved $180 million in COGS, and vendor programs cover 65% of volume. Headwinds like 18% site discounts compressed margins 80 basis points, and returns stayed at 22%. North America hit 46.2%, Europe 41.5%, APAC 37.8% amid competition. For FY24, we guide 43-44%, with dynamic pricing AI adding 150 basis points.

Operating expenses were $1.45 billion, representing 63% of revenue, up just 8% year-over-year despite 22% revenue growth, driving adjusted operating margin to 12.5% from 8.2%. We're honing efficiency across fulfillment, marketing, and tech. Fulfillment at $610 million or 28% of revenue saw per-unit costs drop 15% to $4.20 shipping and $1.80 warehousing, or 12.8% of GMV. Automation with 500 AMRs boosted pick rates 35%, labor to 6.2% of GMV, and returns processing costs fell 12%. North America at 11.5% of GMV, APAC higher at 15.2% from disruptions.

Sales and marketing at $320 million, 14% of revenue, held CAC at $28 with LTV:CAC at 15:1. Performance channels like Google and Meta hit 8.5x ROAS, internalized affiliates cut commissions 15%. Tech and content up 18% to $280 million for AI recs driving 38% of GMV, G&A down 5% via headcount optimization. Targeting 61% OpEx in Q3, 58% by FY25 with robotics, gen AI pricing, and sustainability fleets.

Marketing spend details tie into our campaign effectiveness on brand awareness and acquisition. Total spend $52 million, up 14%, blended ROAS 4.7x. Brand recall up 13% to 48%, unaided 28% among 18-34s from SphereStyle campaign with 2.1 billion impressions. SOV to 8.2% in apparel, EMV $15 million from influencers. Acquired 2.8 million new customers, CAC down 17% to $23.50. Performance marketing 4.9x ROAS on Google, 5.2x Meta; social commerce 42% of acquisitions at 6.1x. Cohorts project $285 CLV. NA 62% of new, APAC +45%, gen AI via Adobe Sensei cut waste 18%. Q2 guide 25-30% new growth at $22 CAC.

Diving into active buyer count growth, our base hit 28.7 million, +22% YoY, +7% QoQ, outpacing eMarketer's 12-15%. Added 5.2 million net new, 28% YoY surge, CAC to $14.80, 22% of LTV at 4.5x. Paid social 45% of new at 3.2x ROAS via TikTok and Meta, organic 30% up 42% post-site migration, partnerships 25% via Walmart and Shopee. NA 52%, APAC +38%, EMEA +25%. Retention 68% at 90 days for new buyers, 64% annualized, ARPU $142. AI personalization +22% add-to-cart, NovaPrime 12.5 million subs at 85% renewal, omnichannel 78%. Guide 6-8 million new in Q3.

Order frequency reached 4.8 per active customer, +18% YoY, +7% QoQ, driving 72% repeat GMV. Subscriptions 28% of orders, MaxRepeat LTV +35%; micro-purchases with 45% same-day; personalization +14% frequency. NA 5.3, APAC 4.9. Targeting 5.5 by FY25 with gen AI nudges, social commerce.

Seller services and VAS at $4.2 billion, +28% YoY, 32% of revenue. 2.8 million active sellers, 68% VAS adoption. FBS 52%, $1.8 billion; ads $1.6 billion at 4.2x ACOS; payments $450 million. NA 72% adoption, APAC +35%. VAS expands margins to 47.2%, 60% of op income.

On seasonality, Q2 GMV $7.4 billion beat by 5% via AI surges, but Q4 guide accounts for peaks at 42% annual GMV. Deviations from macro, with tech flattening curves.

Net income was $180 million, or $0.85 per share. Cash balance $1.2 billion. Reaffirming full-year guidance of $9.5-10 billion revenue, 20-22% growth.

Now I'll turn it over to Lisa Patel to discuss operations.

Lisa Patel:
Thanks, Michael. Operationally, we focused on fulfillment automation and regional logistics expansion. Our shipping times improved by 25%. Fulfillment costs per unit fell 15%. We are implementing robotic systems and micro-fulfillment hubs across key markets.

Now I'll turn it over to David Kim.

David Kim:
Thanks, Lisa. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from our SphereStyle integrated campaign and TikTok Shop lives. Customer acquisition costs stabilized at $23. Our brand awareness increased by 13% per Nielsen. We are focusing on upper-funnel brand building and social commerce to sustain organic growth.

Now I'll turn it over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, David. On the technology front, we've been focused on headless commerce migration and AI personalization engines. Our website uptime was 99.99%. Mobile app usage increased by 35%. We're investing in gen AI for dynamic bidding and server-side tracking.

Now I'll turn it over to Raj Singh.

Raj Singh:
Thanks, Elena. Data science is a key focus for us. We've seen a 22% improvement in conversion rates because of our ML recommendation initiatives. We are also focusing on first-party data platforms and privacy compliance ahead of cookie phaseout.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Instructions for Q&A. Our first question comes from Johnathan Hale with Goldman Sachs.

Johnathan Hale:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Michael, can you expand on the active buyer growth drivers, especially retention in APAC?

Sarah Thompson:
Thanks, Johnathan. Sarah here. Michael covered the headline 22% growth well, but on APAC retention at 55%, we're addressing logistics fragmentation with Cainiao and drone pilots. Our AI engine and NovaPrime perks are pushing cohorts toward 65%, aligning with our flywheel.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen:
Great, thanks. On marketing effectiveness, David or Michael, how sustainable is the CAC decline with rising CPMs?

Michael Chen:
Emily, thanks. The 17% CAC drop to $23.50 comes from ML bidding and first-party data via Snowflake, offsetting 15% CPM hikes. Blended 4.7x ROAS holds, with social at 6.1x. Q3 stable at $22 as we shift to upper-funnel.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Kline with JPMorgan.

Robert Kline:
Thanks. Lisa, on op ex efficiency, any color on fulfillment robotics rollout?

Lisa Patel:
Robert, fulfillment at 12.8% of GMV improved via 500 AMRs boosting picks 35%, labor down 22%. Expanding to 75% capacity by Q4 for another 10% cut, supporting 58% OpEx target.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sophia Grant with Barclays.

Sophia Grant:
Solid results. David, thoughts on order frequency trends and subscription impact?

David Kim:
Sophia, 4.8 frequency up 18% ties to subscriptions at 28% of orders, lifting LTV 35%. MaxRepeat and quick-commerce habits drive repeats, targeting 5.5 FY25 with AI nudges.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Carlos Ruiz with RBC Capital.

Carlos Ruiz:
Thanks. Elena, on seller services adoption, what's driving VAS acceleration?

Elena Vasquez:
Carlos, 68% adoption up from 55%, FBS at 52% with 35% conversion lift, ads 61% at 4.2x. SellerOS 2.0 and APIs boosted uptake 14%, now 32% of revenue at 75% margins.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Priya Patel with Deutsche Bank.

Priya Patel:
Appreciate it. Raj, gross margin details—any regional risks?

Raj Singh:
Priya, 43.8% expansion from mix and ops, but APAC at 37.8% from competition. Hedging with private labels to 40%+, dynamic pricing adds 150 bps FY24.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
